advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make `--rebuild` label unadjudicated flagged items as `UNADJUDICATED` (or fail loudly) instead of defaulting to `TP`, so precision cannot be self-inflated without human adjudication.
evidence: operator_attested_eval.py:127: `adjudications.append({**f, "label": a["label"] if a else "TP", "reason": a["reason"] if a else ""})`
Docstring claim (line ~24): 'Precision ground-truth is a frozen per-item TP/FP adjudication' — but new items are labeled TP without adjudication.

After --rebuild, `prior` is reassigned to the freshly-written result (line 151), so the subsequent reproducibility drift-check (lines 163-173) compares the detector against its own auto-TP labels and cannot detect the inflation.
advisory.finding: `_rebuild` defaults every flagged item lacking a prior adjudication to `label="TP"` (with an empty reason), so any future detector change that flags NEW items has those items auto-scored as true positives on `--rebuild` — inflating precision and defeating the 'frozen per-item TP/FP adjudication' precision gate the eval claims to enforce.
scenarios: A maintainer broadens a marker regex, `--rebuild` flags 20 new borderline items, all get label TP, precision stays ~92% and the gate passes with no human review.
advisory.suggested_fix: In `_rebuild`, use `"label": a["label"] if a else "UNADJUDICATED"` and treat UNADJUDICATED as neither TP nor FP; since `_compute`'s verdict already requires `unadjudicated == 0`, this forces an explicit human label before the gate can PASS.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Report precision over the adjudicated denominator (`tp/(tp+fp)`) and surface `unadjudicated` separately so the printed precision is unambiguous.
evidence: operator_attested_eval.py:94: `precision = round(100 * tp / len(flagged), 1) if flagged else 0.0`
operator_attested_eval.py:85-93: `tp + fp + unadjudicated == len(flagged)` (unadjudicated is a distinct bucket)
Only benign in the PASS path because the verdict requires `unadjudicated == 0` (line 102), but the CLI still prints this precision on FAIL/incomplete runs.
advisory.finding: Precision is computed as `tp / len(flagged)` where `len(flagged)` includes unadjudicated items counted as neither tp nor fp, so a run with unadjudicated flags prints an UNDERSTATED precision that does not equal tp/(tp+fp); the printed 'precision' line is misleading whenever adjudication is incomplete.
scenarios: A run with new unadjudicated flags prints 'precision: 59/80 = 73.8%' when the adjudicated precision is 59/64 = 92.2%, confusing an operator diagnosing a FAIL.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a gating unit test for `_operator_evidence_ac_gaps` (fires on a marker-carrying untagged AC, is suppressed by an in-repo co-signal / negation, and skips an already-`[operator-attested]` item), mirroring `tests/unit/test_gate_eval_classifier.py`'s importlib-load-and-pin convention.
evidence: `search_files` for `_operator_evidence_ac_gaps` under `tests/` returns no matches; the only hits are det_floor.py:715 (def) and the harness.
det_floor.py:715 `def _operator_evidence_ac_gaps(text: str) -> list[tuple[str, list[str]]]:` is a non-trivial detector (marker families, `_OPERATOR_EVIDENCE_SUPPRESS`, `_OPERATOR_EVIDENCE_NEGATION`).
`tests/unit/test_det_invariants.py` covers the sibling p6 verify-command lint (test_verify_command_lint, lines 297-324) but has no case for the operator-evidence detector.
ABSENCE: no `.github/workflows/*.yml` references `plan-review-gate` or `experiments` (search returned no matches), and the Makefile has no `harnesses` reference — so the harness does not gate.
advisory.finding: The new deterministic detector `det_floor._operator_evidence_ac_gaps` — the core new behavior of this change — has no gating regression test. Its only exerciser, `operator_attested_eval.py`, lives under `docs/experiments/` and is invoked by no CI workflow or Makefile target, so a regression in the marker lexicon, suppression co-signal, or negation guard would not be caught by `make test`.
scenarios: A future edit to a `_OPERATOR_EVIDENCE_MARKERS` regex silently stops firing on a real operational-evidence AC (a recall regression) — the untagged 115b/8c4f-class gap re-appears at plan time with no failing test.
A suppression-cosignal regex is broadened and starts swallowing genuine gaps (precision drift) with no unit test to catch it.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `tests/unit/test_operator_evidence_lint.py` that imports `_operator_evidence_ac_gaps` directly and asserts: (a) a `deployed to prod`/`landed via Gerrit` untagged AC returns a gap with the expected marker names; (b) the same AC tagged `[operator-attested]` returns `[]`; (c) an AC carrying a `pytest`/`grep -q` proving command is suppressed; (d) the known 115b/8c4f-style lines fire. This gates in `make test` without the docs-harness.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the harness drift check to also compare the recomputed flagged-set membership (by (ticket_id, ac_text)) and recall against the committed result JSON.
evidence: operator_attested_eval.py:164-170 the drift list only appends on `precision`, `flag_rate`, and `verdict` mismatch.
The recomputed `c['flagged']` membership and `recall_pct` are printed (lines 155-157) but never asserted against the committed `prior`.
advisory.finding: The self-gate harness's reproducibility drift check asserts only `precision_pct`, `flag_rate_pct`, and `verdict` match the committed JSON — it does not compare the flagged-set membership or recall, so a change that swaps which AC items fire while keeping the same flagged count and precision would pass the drift check undetected.
scenarios: A marker regex is retuned so a false positive is dropped and a different false positive is gained at the same count/precision — the committed flagged census silently no longer matches the shipped detector, yet drift reports clean.
